findings.summary: N30V7-F05 (routed here from N30_PREFLIGHT_EGRESS attempt-1, BLOCKED): transport.observe_codex_identity could not extract an executed model from the real, installed Codex CLI's actual --json exec event stream (codex-cli 0.147.0; thread.started/turn.started/item.completed/turn.completed never carry a model field on any variant, live-verified). Root cause: the pinned invocation's own --ephemeral flag suppresses the one machine-readable Codex receipt that does carry the executed model -- the on-disk rollout file's turn_context.payload.model. Fix, scoped entirely to N20's write set (runtime/langgraph_factory/transport.py, tests/runtime/test_plan26_transport.py): build_codex_argv drops --ephemeral; observe_codex_identity now binds this exact invocation's stdout thread.started.thread_id to exactly one rollout file under codex_home whose own session_meta.payload.session_id matches, and reads that file's final turn_context.payload.model (last one wins, mirroring the existing reroute-supersedes-initial rule already used for Claude identity). Zero or multiple rollout matches are refused as an unobservable identity, never guessed by mtime or path recency -- load-bearing because the driver-capability preflight probe (N30-owned runtime/run_curriculum.py, unchanged call contract, now passed an explicit codex_home) deliberately runs against the operator's real, shared ~/.codex, which can hold rollout files from unrelated, concurrent, or historical invocations. New observe_identity(..., codex_home=...) parameter added; the one production call site (CliTransport._attempt) passes workspace.home / 'codex', the same disposable per-activation CODEX_HOME build_worker_environment already establishes for every real job.

Deterministic positive and negative regression proof added (tests/runtime/test_plan26_transport.py): identity reads the rollout file bound by thread_id (positive); reroute's later turn_context supersedes the initial one and correctly raises IdentityMismatch against a stale decided model (positive); the real captured codex-cli 0.147.0 stdout shape alone (no thread_id or no matching rollout) still fails closed (negative, two variants); and -- the specific proof the routing instruction required -- an unrelated, concurrent rollout file for a different thread_id under the same codex_home is never mistaken for the invoked process, plus zero-match and multiple-match (ambiguous binding) are both explicitly refused rather than guessed. 7/7 new/updated identity tests pass in isolation; full N20 verification suite (464 passed, 1 skipped, 140 subtests) is unaffected.

Live-verified against the genuinely installed codex-cli 0.147.0 (not simulated): runtime.run_curriculum._prove_driver_capabilities() now reports the codex driver's observable_subscription_backed_usability as PASS (observed_model: gpt-5.6-sol) and overall ready: true, where it previously reported FAIL/malformed_or_unobservable_output (N30V7-F05 evidence, 04_live_driver_capability_proof.log under N30's prior attempt-1). N20V7-F01 through F03 (write-set/scan-scope conformance, prior graph-v5 implementation, test-count parity) remain resolved and unaffected -- production code touched by this attempt is limited to the one function family this finding names.
